historical_references.reference: According to tradition, St. Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, was the first Bishop of Rome. He is believed to have been crucified upside down during the reign of Emperor Nero around AD 64. The name 'Petrian' may have originated from this historical figure.

The name 'Petrian' may also have been used in the Middle Ages, specifically during the Crusades, to refer to someone who was a member of the military order known as the Knights Templar. These knights were called 'Poor Knights of Christ and the Temple of Solomon' and took the name 'Petrian' from the biblical figure St. Peter, who was considered their patron saint.
